root_idea.summary: The root centers on going forth or extending through open space, especially movement across the land.
root_idea.development: From movement through the land, the vocabulary develops into terms for herds and groups, roads and passages, flowing or leaking water, and things that extend or run along a surface.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested active participle is a distinct lexical form.
The Quran-attested noun meaning mirage is a distinct lexical form.
The Quran-attested noun or verbal noun in 18:61 has a distinct passage and going-away usage.

senses.definition: Going forth or moving along one's way; in the Quranic expression, one who is out or appearing by day.
senses.usage_conditions: In 13:10, it is contrasted with one who hides by night. The expression is also understood as going along the roads or course by day.

senses.definition: A mirage: a bright semblance of water seen across the land, especially a midday appearance that has no actual water.
senses.usage_conditions: In 24:39 it occurs in a simile for an apparent but unreal object of expectation; in 78:20 it describes the mountains when they are made to appear as a mirage.

senses.definition: A hidden or subterranean passage or place, such as a burrow or an underground way.
senses.usage_conditions: In 18:61, the fish's route into the sea is interpreted as a passage or place resembling a subterranean excavation or hidden way.

senses.definition: Going away or taking a downward or onward course; a way taken through a place.
senses.usage_conditions: In 18:61, the word is also explained as the fish's going away or taking its way into the sea. This is a verbal-noun use rather than the name of a physical passage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go forth or go away into the land, or to go about accomplishing one's need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb with the infinitive سُرُوبٌ; the expression may describe movement through the country or going about during the day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wander or go away at random into the country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an explicitly reported extension of going forth without a fixed destination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, cattle, or a stallion camel, to go out freely to pasture or to the grazing place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of livestock or a stallion that leads or accompanies the herd to pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, a spring, a waterskin, or a mirage, to flow or run; of a waterskin, to leak through its seams.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The water may run over the ground, flow from a source, or escape through punctures in a sewn skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sew a waterskin or similar skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated verbal noun سَرْبٌ is also used for the sewing itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become affected by constipation through the penetrating fumes of molten lead or silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare passive-form lexical usage, reported of a man who may recover or die from the condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send camels, horsemen, people, or things in a group or successively; to send someone back by the way he came.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sending may be party after party, portion after portion, or one thing after another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a subterranean excavation; of a digger, to dig a well toward the right and left.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes lateral underground digging rather than ordinary surface excavation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour water into a new waterskin so that its sewing cord swells and seals the punctures.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The action is performed to make the skin watertight by moistening the thong used in sewing it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make water flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To follow one another continuously along a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people or things proceeding successively through a route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become full of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form V usage, distinct from causing a waterskin to be filled or sealed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter into a subterranean habitation, burrow, or other place of concealment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a wild animal or fox entering its underground abode.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pasturing livestock; livestock that pasture during the day without a herder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote the act of pasturing or the camels and cattle engaged in it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sheepfold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported nominal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way, road, or course; the unobstructed way in which someone goes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It occurs in expressions meaning to leave someone's way free or to release a captive to proceed freely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bosom, breast, or mind; breadth of mind, judgment, or disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression وَاسِعُ السَّرْبِ, it can describe an ample-minded person, including one slow to anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A herd, flock, or group of animals; by extension, a group of women or men, birds, or a collection of palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is applied to gazelles, wild cattle, wild asses, sheep and goats, birds, and other grouped creatures; the human applications are figurative or extended.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way, road, or course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the kasra-vowelled form reported as synonymous with سَرْبٌ in the sense of a way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state or condition, especially ease or spaciousness of mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In وَاسِعُ السِّرْبِ, it can describe someone in an unstraitened condition or slow to anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart, mind, or self; in idiomatic use, one's household, family, property, or people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In آمِنٌ فِي سِرْبِهِ, authorities variously explain the referent as one's inner self, household, property, or people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A subterranean channel or conduit by which water enters a garden or walled palm garden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a water-engineering sense, distinct from the hidden passage described in the Quranic occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flowing water, including water escaping from a waterskin or from holes in its sewing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may describe water running freely or dripping through punctures in a leather container.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water put into a new waterskin so that its sewing cord becomes moist, swells, and closes the holes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This names the preparatory water used to make a newly sewn skin watertight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flowing or leaking water; a waterskin that is leaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is applied to water and to a leather water container that allows water to escape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single puncture or stitch-hole in a skin or similar object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source explicitly questions the vowel and proposes that this meaning may belong under سُرْبَةٌ; the form is therefore retained with that lexical uncertainty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short journey; a way, course, mode, or manner of proceeding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may describe taking a near or distant way, or pursuing a particular course of action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion or detached group of a larger herd or collection; specifically, a group of horses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The group of horses is variously reported as numbering roughly ten to thirty; the broader sense includes a detached portion of gazelles, birds, sheep, or similar animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company of men who leave an army to make a hostile incursion and return.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized military sense of a detached company.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A row or line, including a row of grapevines.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense extends to any orderly row or line.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seam, stitch, puncture, or stitch-hole in a skin or similar object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a noun for the result or component of sewing a leather container.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The proper name of the she-camel associated with al-Basūs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An indeclinable or imperfectly declinable proper name in a proverbial expression; it is unrelated to the ordinary noun meaning mirage except in form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Accustomed to go away at random.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive or adjectival derivative describing one habitually wandering or departing without fixed direction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sheep or goat that is driven back from water after drinking and followed by the flock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for the animal that leads the return from the watering place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Going away freely or at random into the country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader Classical usage is distinct from the Quranic contextual contrast of hiding by night and going forth by day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Going to pasture; of camels, cattle, or a stallion camel, repairing to the grazing place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also applied to a gazelle going away in its grazing place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lead, or a related dark metallic substance such as black lead, tin, or pewter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized loanword, with أُسْرُبٌّ reported as the more common form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fumes of molten lead or silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized material sense associated with the Arabicized metal term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way or route; also a place where livestock go to pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived noun can denote either the route itself or the pasture-place toward which livestock go.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A channel of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be used literally of a watercourse or figuratively of channels from which tears flow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The passage and outlet of dung, or the upper part of the anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical usage with reported vowel variation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sitting place like a raised platform before a chamber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source distinguishes it from a chamber itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The narrow line or growth of hair descending from the breast toward the navel or pubes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported extent ranges from the middle of the chest to the pubic region; the term can also mean the chest hair generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The soft parts of an animal's belly, including the groins and related areas.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the plural مَسَارِب, the term refers to soft or lower body regions of beasts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Very tall when applied to a man, or very long when applied to hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival usage describing extended height or length.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Editorial correction of a lexicographical citation.
Additional successive-sending constructions are covered by the same sending branch.
The well-digging construction specifies the same subterranean excavation branch.
Editorial transition to phrases cited elsewhere.
The entry records this lexical claim while noting a possible correction of the vowel.
The way, course, and mode expressions belong to the same journey/course branch.
The horse-company specification is covered by the detached-group meaning.
The cross-reference is lexical and the derivative meaning is retained.
Pointer to the final sentence of another entry.

cautions: The Quranic use of سَرَبٌ in 18:61 has closely related but materially different lexical interpretations: a hidden or subterranean passage and the act of going away or taking a course. These are retained as separate senses.
Some Classical entries preserve reported vowel or reading uncertainty, especially سَرْبَةٌ in the stitch-hole sense; that uncertainty is stated in the relevant usage conditions.
